title: Fixed-width integer types and format macros from stdint.h/inttypes.h
learningObjectives: Distinguish exact-width, minimum-width and fastest-width integer typedefs and identify optional versus guaranteed types.
Choose integer types based on protocol, storage, range and performance requirements instead of assuming int has a fixed size.
Use inttypes.h macros such as PRId32, PRIuLEAST32 and SCNdLEAST32 with matching argument types.
Explain integer promotions and risks of mixing signed and unsigned values.
Use limits and compile-time checks to document genuine representation assumptions.
Build portable examples that print, parse and validate integer values.

understand.concept: stdint.h defines integer typedefs with specified width properties. Exact-width types such as int32_t and uint64_t are optional: they exist only when a suitable exact-width type is available. Minimum-width types such as int_least32_t express a required minimum range. Fastest-width types such as int_fast32_t express a minimum width while allowing an implementation-preferred efficient type. inttypes.h supplies matching format and scanning macros.
understand.whyItMatters: int is not guaranteed to be 32 bits, and a typedef's underlying type can differ across implementations. Matching format specifiers prevents variadic argument mismatches and portability defects in protocols and numeric processing.
understand.analogy: A portable C interface is a contract between source code and the implementation.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the exact C standard and implementation guarantees.

explain.narrative: Choose exact-width types when an external representation truly requires that width and the type exists. Choose least-width types when a minimum range is enough. Use ordinary int when no fixed representation is needed. Include inttypes.h and write formats such as "%" PRId32; the macro expands to the correct conversion fragment. The same principle applies to SCN macros and pointer arguments. Small integer types may undergo integer promotions. Mixing signed and unsigned operands can convert a negative value to a large unsigned value. Validate ranges before narrowing conversions. Use limit macros and _Static_assert when a genuine representation requirement must be enforced.

examples.title: Print minimum-width integers portably
examples.explanation: Minimum-width types express required ranges without assuming the underlying type. Matching inttypes macros provide the correct printf conversion.

examples.title: Read an integer with the matching scan macro
examples.explanation: SCNdLEAST32 matches the pointer type supplied to scanf. The return count is checked before the value is used. Production input may use strtoimax for stricter trailing-text and range policies.

practise.guidedTask: Print signed and unsigned minimum-width values using matching macros, then explain why exact-width typedefs are optional.
practise.independentTask: Design a record field for a binary protocol. State whether exact-width support is mandatory, validate the value before conversion and use the correct format macro for diagnostics.
hints: Check bounds before accessing array elements.
Validate external text before conversion or use.
Use the matching standard-library interface and type.
Test normal, boundary and invalid-input cases.
Record implementation-specific assumptions instead of guessing.

questions.prompt: Which statement about int32_t is correct?
options: It is optional and exists only when an implementation supports an exact 32-bit signed integer type without padding bits.
It is guaranteed on every conforming C implementation.
questions.answer: It is optional and exists only when an implementation supports an exact 32-bit signed integer type without padding bits.
questions.explanation: Exact-width typedefs are optional; minimum-width typedefs serve programs that need at least a specified range.

questions.prompt: Why use PRId32 with an int32_t argument?
options: The macro provides the printf conversion fragment matching the implementation's int32_t underlying type.
It converts the integer to a string before printf.
It forces int32_t to be 32 bits.
questions.answer: The macro provides the printf conversion fragment matching the implementation's int32_t underlying type.
questions.explanation: The matching macro avoids assuming a particular underlying type for a variadic argument.

options: A signed integer type with at least the required 32-bit value range.
An object exactly four bytes on every platform.
questions.answer: A signed integer type with at least the required 32-bit value range.
questions.explanation: Least-width types guarantee a minimum range while allowing a wider underlying representation.

questions.prompt: Which header defines PRI and SCN format macro families?
questions.explanation: inttypes.h provides portable formatted I/O macros for integer typedef families.

questions.prompt: What risk arises when a negative signed value is compared with an unsigned value?
options: The signed value may be converted to unsigned, producing a large value.
The unsigned value always becomes negative.
questions.answer: The signed value may be converted to unsigned, producing a large value.
questions.explanation: Usual arithmetic conversions can convert a negative signed operand to unsigned, changing the comparison result.
